URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/20/uk-prime-minister-burnham-trump-poverty-stricken-disaster.html
(CNBC + NPR/CNN context, search snippets, week of 20-27 July 2026)

- Andy Burnham, 56, became the UK's seventh prime minister in just over a decade on 20 July 2026, succeeding Keir Starmer; the fourth PM of King Charles III's reign.
- Burnham began by reshuffling the cabinet, removing several allies of his predecessor, and outlined a 10-year national plan to tackle the cost-of-living crisis and revive the economy.
- He pledged immediate relief for households struggling with rising costs, saying the first measures would be announced on Tuesday.
- Challenges inherited: sluggish growth, high borrowing costs, rising welfare spending and pressure over irregular migration fuelling support for Reform UK.
